status.note: Chosen to test whether one navigation gap serves two components. Uses cardinality: one, like RadioGroup, and needs the same arrow-key model — but its members come in TWO kinds, a tab and a panel, which collection.items cannot say.

intent.purpose: Holds which one of several sections is showing, in a fixed area, so a person can move between them without losing their place on the page.
behaviour: Holds exactly one selected value. Unlike an accordion, the selection can never be emptied — there is always a visible panel.
Renders its tabs inside a tablist and its panels as siblings of it, because a tablist may contain only tabs.
Moves between tabs on the arrow keys, wrapping at both ends, and selects as it moves.
Keeps exactly one tab in the Tab order, so Tab enters the strip and then leaves it for the panel.
notFor: Navigation between routes. These panels show and hide in place; nothing here changes the URL or manages history.
Content that should all be readable at once. Tabs hide everything but one panel, which makes comparing them impossible and makes find-in-page miss most of the content.
More sections than fit on one line. A wrapping or scrolling tab strip is a different design with different keyboard rules.
A filter strip with no panels. Without panels this is not the tabs pattern — use a radio group or a nav, which say what they actually do.

disabled.description: The whole strip ignores interaction. Cascades to every tab.
disabled.visual: Every tab dims and none can be chosen.

a11y.keyboard: Tab enters the strip on the selected tab and leaves it for the panel. Arrow keys move between tabs and select as they move, wrapping at both ends.
notes: The tablist has no accessible name of its own. A consumer must supply one via aria-label or aria-labelledby, or assistive technology announces an unnamed set of tabs.

Selection follows focus, which suits panels already in memory and is the wrong default for a panel that fetches. That distinction is a real design decision and this contract cannot express which was chosen.
Exactly one tab is reachable with Tab. A controlled value matching no rendered tab leaves the whole strip unreachable by keyboard, and nothing here detects it.
Content hidden in an unselected panel is invisible to find-in-page. That is the cost of the pattern and no option here mitigates it.

children.description: The tabs and the panels. TabItems become the strip; TabPanels are rendered after it.

root.description: The wrapper holding the strip and the panels, so the two stay adjacent and can be positioned as a pair.

list.description: The strip itself. Owns the arrow-key movement and the single Tab stop.
